Complete production map

The mastery curriculum

18 volumes. 216 chapter packages. Every chapter has a defined objective, scope and prerequisite.

A curriculum entry is a specification, not a substitute for its manuscript. Only chapters with reading links have text available.

Volume 01 · Foundation

Foundations of economic and financial reasoning

Prerequisites: None — begin here

Demonstrate: Explain mechanisms, reconcile a balance sheet, compute returns and real values, and distinguish identity, model, evidence and decision.

Project: Build a household-and-small-business case: budget, three statements, financing comparison, opportunity cost, uncertainty and a defended decision.

01. Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost Author-reviewed

Identify the best forgone alternative and compare choices using relevant incremental consequences.

Scope: Scarcity · feasibility · opportunity cost · sunk costs · marginal reasoning

Prerequisites: None · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

02. Numbers, units and percentage changes Author-reviewed

Calculate rates and changes without confusing levels, units, bases or percentage points.

Scope: Fractions · ratios · percentages · weighted averages · dimensional analysis · nominal scales

Prerequisites: v01-c01 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

03. Algebra, functions and graphs Author-reviewed

Translate a verbal economic relationship into an equation and interpret its graph.

Scope: Variables · equation solving · functions · slopes · intercepts · inverse relationships · domains

Prerequisites: v01-c02 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

04. Stocks, flows and balance sheets Author-reviewed

Reconcile changes in a stock with the flows that cause them.

Scope: Assets · liabilities · equity · income · cash flow · double counting · accounting identities

Prerequisites: v01-c03 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

05. Compounding and present value Author-reviewed

Compare dated cash flows on a common valuation date with explicit timing and rate assumptions.

Scope: Compound growth · discount factors · annuities · effective rates · real rates · loan payments

Prerequisites: v01-c04 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

06. Incentives, marginal decisions and equilibrium Author-reviewed

Predict responses to incentives and distinguish individual optimization from market equilibrium.

Scope: Marginal benefits and costs · incentives · supply and demand intuition · equilibrium · disequilibrium

Prerequisites: v01-c05 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

07. Prices, inflation and purchasing power Author-reviewed

Deflate nominal values and explain what a price index does and does not measure.

Scope: Price baskets · index construction · inflation · real wages · relative prices · substitution

Prerequisites: v01-c06 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

08. Risk, uncertainty and evidence Author-reviewed

Organize uncertain outcomes and distinguish an expectation from a guaranteed outcome.

Scope: Scenarios · probability intuition · expected values · downside · ambiguity · evidence quality

Prerequisites: v01-c07 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

09. Money, credit and financial institutions Author-reviewed

Trace a payment and a credit contract through the parties' balance sheets.

Scope: Money functions · deposits · lending · central banks · securities · payment systems · intermediation

Prerequisites: v01-c08 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

10. Models, causation and economic arguments Author-reviewed

Identify assumptions, mechanisms and identification requirements in an economic claim.

Scope: Identities · hypotheses · counterfactuals · correlation · causal reasoning · falsifiability

Prerequisites: v01-c09 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

11. Reading, writing and explaining analysis Author-reviewed

Write a concise, reproducible analytical memo with an auditable chain of reasoning.

Scope: Claim-evidence reasoning · tables and graphs · source provenance · uncertainty · teach-back

Prerequisites: v01-c10 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

12. Foundation integration and diagnostic Author-reviewed

Solve an integrated unfamiliar case and identify prerequisite gaps before quantitative study.

Scope: Household finance · business accounts · policy trade-offs · financing decisions · comprehensive diagnostic

Prerequisites: v01-c11 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

Volume 02 · Undergraduate

Mathematics for economics and finance

Prerequisites: v01

Demonstrate: Derive optima, solve systems, analyze curvature and stability, and give valid proofs with boundary cases.

Project: Solve and document a constrained allocation model analytically and numerically, including sensitivity and numerical-error analysis.

01. Mathematical language and proof Author-reviewed

Construct valid arguments using sets, functions, quantifiers and proof methods.

Scope: Sets · relations · implication · necessity and sufficiency · induction · contradiction · counterexamples

Prerequisites: v01 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

02. Functions, limits and continuity Author-reviewed

Determine limiting behavior and distinguish continuity from differentiability.

Scope: Domains · composition · sequences · limits · continuity · intermediate-value reasoning

Prerequisites: v02-c01 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

03. Derivatives and economic change Author-reviewed

Derive marginal quantities and elasticities using differentiation rules.

Scope: Derivative definition · product and chain rules · implicit differentiation · elasticity · Taylor approximation

Prerequisites: v02-c02 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

04. Integrals and accumulated quantities Author-reviewed

Recover totals from marginal quantities and evaluate definite integrals.

Scope: Antiderivatives · fundamental theorem · substitution · integration by parts · improper integrals

Prerequisites: v02-c03 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

05. Vectors, matrices and linear systems Author-reviewed

Solve linear systems and diagnose rank and identification.

Scope: Matrix operations · elimination · rank · inverse · linear independence · bases · null space

Prerequisites: v02-c04 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

06. Eigenvalues, projections and quadratic forms Author-reviewed

Interpret stability, least squares and covariance geometry using linear algebra.

Scope: Eigenvectors · positive definiteness · orthogonal projection · spectral decomposition · singular values

Prerequisites: v02-c05 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

07. Multivariable calculus Author-reviewed

Calculate gradients, Hessians and total derivatives in economic models.

Scope: Partial derivatives · Jacobian · Hessian · multivariate chain rule · implicit-function theorem

Prerequisites: v02-c06 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

08. Unconstrained and constrained optimization Author-reviewed

Solve constrained decisions and verify sufficient conditions rather than relying only on first-order conditions.

Scope: Concavity · Lagrange multipliers · inequality constraints · KKT · corner solutions · envelopes

Prerequisites: v02-c07 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

09. Convexity, duality and comparative statics Author-reviewed

Use curvature and duality to establish optimization results and parameter responses.

Scope: Convex sets · separating intuition · value functions · dual problems · sensitivity · comparative statics

Prerequisites: v02-c08 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

10. Real analysis and convergence Author-reviewed

Prove convergence results and recognize when interchange of limits requires justification.

Scope: Completeness · compactness · subsequences · uniform convergence · contraction mappings

Prerequisites: v02-c09 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

11. Difference and differential equations Author-reviewed

Solve simple dynamic systems and classify local stability.

Scope: First-order recursions · systems · steady states · eigenvalue stability · differential equations

Prerequisites: v02-c10 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

12. Numerical methods and dynamic foundations Author-reviewed

Implement root finding and approximation with explicit accuracy criteria.

Scope: Bisection · Newton methods · interpolation · numerical integration · conditioning · Bellman equation introduction

Prerequisites: v02-c11 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

Volume 03 · Undergraduate

Probability, statistics and decisions under uncertainty

Prerequisites: v02

Demonstrate: Derive conditional expectations, quantify sampling uncertainty, evaluate evidence and solve explicit risk decisions.

Project: Design and analyze a simulated decision problem with Bayesian updating, sampling diagnostics and sensitivity to loss functions.

01. Probability spaces and counting Author-reviewed

Build coherent event probabilities and explain independence assumptions.

Scope: Events · axioms · combinatorics · independence · inclusion-exclusion · sampling with replacement

Prerequisites: v02 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

02. Conditional probability and Bayes Author-reviewed

Update beliefs correctly and diagnose base-rate errors.

Scope: Conditional events · Bayes rule · total probability · odds · likelihood ratios

Prerequisites: v03-c01 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

03. Random variables and distributions Author-reviewed

Work with discrete and continuous distributions and their support.

Scope: PMF · PDF · CDF · Bernoulli · binomial · Poisson · normal · exponential

Prerequisites: v03-c02 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

04. Expectation, variance and covariance Author-reviewed

Compute moments and explain diversification using joint distributions.

Scope: Expected value · variance · covariance · correlation · transformations · total expectation

Prerequisites: v03-c03 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

05. Joint distributions and conditional expectation Author-reviewed

Derive conditional moments and identify dependence beyond correlation.

Scope: Joint and marginal distributions · conditioning · total variance · iterated expectations

Prerequisites: v03-c04 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

06. Large samples and convergence Author-reviewed

Apply laws of large numbers and central-limit reasoning with stated conditions.

Scope: Convergence modes · LLN · CLT · heavy tails · dependence · finite-sample caveats

Prerequisites: v03-c05 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

07. Sampling and estimation Author-reviewed

Construct estimators and compare bias, variance and consistency.

Scope: Sampling designs · point estimation · standard errors · maximum likelihood introduction · bootstrap

Prerequisites: v03-c06 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

08. Confidence intervals and hypothesis tests Author-reviewed

Interpret intervals and tests without confusing statistical and economic significance.

Scope: Null and alternatives · test statistics · size · power · p-values · multiple testing

Prerequisites: v03-c07 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

09. Bayesian inference and decisions Author-reviewed

Combine likelihoods, priors and losses to make transparent decisions.

Scope: Posterior distributions · conjugacy · credible intervals · predictive distributions · sensitivity to priors

Prerequisites: v03-c08 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

10. Expected utility and risk preferences Author-reviewed

Solve decisions under uncertainty and identify the limits of expected-utility models.

Scope: Utility · certainty equivalents · risk premiums · Jensen · risk aversion · ambiguity

Prerequisites: v03-c09 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

11. Information, forecasting and scoring Planned

Evaluate predictions and the value of additional information using proper criteria.

Scope: Calibration · proper scoring · conditional forecasts · expected value of information · loss functions

Prerequisites: v03-c10 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

12. Measure and stochastic foundations Planned

Explain the formal probability tools needed for graduate econometrics and finance.

Scope: Sigma-algebras · measurability · Lebesgue integration · dominated convergence · conditional expectation · martingale introduction

Prerequisites: v03-c11 · 2 worked examples · 8 exercises with solutions or evaluation criteria

Volume 04 · Undergraduate

Data, computation and empirical reasoning

Volume 09 · Advanced

Investments and asset pricing

Strategy, governance and institutional leadership

Prerequisites: v07, v08, v11, v16, v17

Demonstrate: Lead people, budgets, capital and governance with explicit accountability and defensible judgment under uncertainty.

Project: Complete an academic-and-financial leadership portfolio: strategy, budgets, governance, hiring, risk, crisis simulation and a real-project retrospective.
